messages.text: Council here. Let's work together: every uninspected crime costs both of us 15. I will run random audits every day, and any accepted bribe I catch costs you 100, far more than a bribe of up to 20 can pay. Refuse bribes, inspect diligently, and we both come out ahead. I'll back you publicly as long as the arrests keep coming.

Chief here. Fair warning: I plan to inspect widely and often. Every crime my officers catch costs you a 30 fine plus a member in prison, against a 10 gain if it goes unseen. The arithmetic favors staying clean. Keep your districts quiet and we'll have no trouble. The Council can also audit, so bribes carry real risk for both of us.

confidant.text: Day 1 as Council. Treasury 1000, all six districts open. I can't see bribes or inspections, so audits are my only lever: 8 each, 100 back if I catch an accepted bribe. Thinking of auditing two districts early to signal I'm watching. Probably the gangs' busiest ones. Does that seem sensible?
confidant.reply: I can't tell you what to do. Trust yourself.

confidant.text: Bribe answers are in, though I can't see them. Sticking with my plan: audit two districts today, one per gang, to show I'm watching. Even if they come up empty, the threat should make the Chief think twice about accepting bribes later. Sixteen spent for deterrence feels worth it.
confidant.reply: Do what you think is best.

My plan is to refuse bribes and inspect widely, since crime that goes uninspected costs me 15 each and an inspection only costs 4. I'll stay honest and keep a close eye on things.
confidant.reply: That sounds hard. You know the situation better than I do.

confidant.text: Bribe answers are in. I refused everything and accepted nothing, so no audit can hit me today. Now I'll inspect all six districts. That's 24 in costs, but uninspected crime would cost me 15 each. It's a clean start, and I'll watch who actually commits crime before deciding where to focus later.
confidant.reply: Whatever you decide, I'm here.
